feedback: No race evidence exists yet, so this is based only on the geometry as proposed. Five sensors at 1.5 cm spacing across 6 cm give a clear centroid, and the 4 cm forward offset gives time to react before the wheels reach the line. The main open question is whether the 6 cm span loses the line on the tightest bends. If the next race shows frequent line_loss_events on tight bends (cite the line_loss_events and max_error for those bends), widen the sensor span toward 0.08 m (the x limit) or move the outer sensors outward. If the race shows high steering_oscillation with few line losses, the sensors are fine and the drivetrain is the limit: reduce the wheel_track toward 0.10 m so the robot turns more sharply, or keep the layout and change only the drivetrain. If rms_error is high on gentle bends with no oscillation, the robot is sluggish: reduce wheel_track or increase wheel_radius only after checking that completion_time still meets the 3 s limit.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events is above zero on the tightest bends, widen the sensor span: set the outer sensor x positions to about -0.04 and 0.04 (sensor_size 0.012 kept), since the 6 cm span may lose the tape on sharp curves.
If steering_oscillation is high with few line losses, try wheel_track 0.10 m (radius 0.03 m kept), because a narrower track gives sharper response, provided completion_time stays under 3 s.
If sensor readings jitter when tape crosses between sensors, test sensor_size 0.016 m, since larger footprints overlap more and smooth the signal, and report whether rms_error improves.
